name: Splenic Diffuse Red Pulp Small B-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Diffuse involvement of the splenic red pulp by small B-cell lymphoma cells
Neoplastic B-cells expressing CD20+, CD79a+, negative for CD5, CD10, and CD23
Bone marrow involvement with intrasinusoidal infiltration pattern
Absence of typical mutations seen in other splenic B-cell lymphomas (e.g., NOTCH2 mutations)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse splenic red pulp involvement by small B-cells with characteristic immunophenotype and bone marrow infiltration
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histopathology, immunophenotyping, and clinical features; exclusion of other splenic B-cell lymphomas is essential.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically painless enlargement of the spleen

searchTerms: bone marrow infiltration within blood sinuses
cancer cells in marrow blood spaces

common.notes: Normocytic, normochromic anemia due to marrow involvement
Low platelet count secondary to splenic sequestration or marrow infiltration
Secondary to chronic disease and cytopenias
searchTerms: fatigue related to low red blood cells

common.notes: Reduced white blood cell count occasionally observed

occasional.notes: B symptoms may be present but less common
Sensation of fullness or early satiety
searchTerms: abdominal fullness due to spleen swelling

occasional.notes: Elevated lymphocyte count in peripheral blood occasionally seen

rare.notes: Rarely present, helps differentiate from other lymphomas

searchTerms: immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing small mature B lymphocytes
Bone marrow biopsy with intrasinusoidal infiltration
Immunophenotyping: CD20+, CD79a+, CD5-, CD10-, CD23-
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing massive splenomegaly without significant lymphadenopathy
genetic: Lack of NOTCH2 and BRAF mutations typical of other splenic B-cell lymphomas
other: Histopathology demonstrating diffuse red pulp infiltration by small B-cells

distinguishingFeatures: CD5 and CD23 negative but often with villous lymphocytes
Expression of CD103, CD25, and CD11c

redFlags: Severe cytopenias causing bleeding or infection
Splenic rupture or acute abdominal pain
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Chott A, et al. Splenic diffuse red pulp small B-cell lymphoma: a distinct entity. Blood. 2006;108(2): 690-697.
